sections.content: BARGAINING UNIT

The Employer recognizes the Union as the sole and exclusive Bargaining Agent for all production, maintenance, shop clerical employees employed in factory areas, and all employees in the job classifications listed in the Appendices of this Agreement and who are employed by its El Segundo, Fullerton, Newport Beach, Torrance, Long Beach, and the Corporate Headquarters located in Los Angeles, CA, and referred to in NLRB certifications and applicable orders and agreements. Excluded from the Bargaining Unit are all supervisors, all administrative, professional, engineering and office employees, confidential employees, all plant protection and security employees, and all Finance Department employees, except timekeepers and maintenance electricians.

ARTICLE I
PERIOD OF AGREEMENT Section A. Effective Date and Period of Agreement

1. This Agreement is effective at 12:01 a.m. May 23, 2005 and supersedes the provisions of the October 19, 2001 through May 23, 2005 Collective Bargaining Agreement in their entirety at that time. This Agreement shall remain in effect for the term commencing on the 23rd day of May 2005 and ending at 12:01 a.m. on the 10th day of May 2008; and thereafter from year to year unless either party notifies the other in writing by hand or overnight delivery of the desire to terminate, amend or modify, in which event the written notice shall be given at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the expiration date of this Agreement.

sections.content: Section B. Amendment or Modification

1. Should negotiations be commenced to amend or modify Articles of this Agreement, the entire Agreement shall be extended and remain in full force and effect during the period of such negotiations, until such time as a complete new Agreement is signed. However, notwithstanding the above, either party shall have the right during any extended period to terminate the Agreement during said extended period by giving the other party written notice by hand or overnight delivery that the right to terminate is being exercised. In this event, the Agreement shall be terminated and void twenty (20) calendar days after receipt by either party of such written notice.

sections.content:
ARTICLE II
GENERAL PROVISIONS Section A. Mutual Pledge of Accord

1. The Union and its members, and the Employer, agree that every good faith effort shall be made to administer this Agreement in accordance with the true intent of its terms and provisions to the end of maintaining sound Labor Relations. The parties hereto intend by this Agreement to provide a stabilized relationship between them and to insure uninterrupted production of quality products on schedule at competitive costs during the life of said Agreement. It is therefore agreed that during the term of this Agreement, or during any agreed extension period thereof, there shall be no lock-out, strike, including sympathy strikes, slow-down, sit-down, work stoppage or other form of job action by the Union or its members, or by the Employer; provided that all claims, disputes or differences arising out of the terms of this Agreement shall be settled in accordance with the procedure provided by this Agreement.

sections.content: Section B. Right to Manage the Plant

1. The management and operation of the Plants, administration of the Employer's business and direction of the working force are exclusive functions of Management. Provided such does not violate other terms of this Agreement, Management shall have the right to increase, decrease or rotate the working force; to hire, promote, demote, discharge or discipline for cause; to transfer or reclassify employees; to originate merit raises and determine merit ratings; to assign personnel to shifts, overtime and special work requirements; to submit for security clearances; to establish work processes, standards, shifts, schedules and methods; to plan, route and schedule production; and, to determine the extent to which the Plants or any unit of the Plants shall be operated or shut down.

ARTICLE III
HOURS OF WORK AND OVERTIME Section A. Workweek and Workday

1. The normal weekly work schedule established by the Employer shall consist of five (5) consecutive working days of eight (8) hours each, Monday through Friday (6-1/2 hours on the graveyard shift) exclusive of meal periods. The workweek shall consist of seven (7) consecutive days beginning at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday and ending at 12:00 midnight on the following Friday.

sections.content: 2. The workday is defined as a twenty-four (24) hour period, beginning at 12:01 a.m. and ending at 12:00 midnight on the same day. sections.content: Section F. Apportionment of Overtime

1. It is the Employer's intention to give as much advance notice as possible when overtime is necessary. It is recognized that occasionally employees may not desire to work a particular assignment. Therefore, when overtime assignments are made, employees who do not desire to work such overtime shall make their reasons known to supervision. If such reasons are acceptable to supervision, in view of production requirements and other circumstances involved, such employees will be excused from the overtime assignment and will not be subject to discipline for declining the overtime, but will be credited on the overtime records for the time not worked. Additionally, if the affected employee is not given notice of an overtime assignment by the end of his/her shift on Thursday for a weekend overtime assignment, or the start of his/her lunch period for a weekday overtime assignment or 72 hours for a holiday assignment, and the employee is unable to work the overtime as a result, he/she will also be excused from the overtime assignment. Such employees will not be subject to discipline for declining the overtime, but will be credited on the overtime records for the time not worked up to a maximum of 40 hours per employee in a six (6) month overtime review interval.

sections.content: ARTICLE VII Section A. Definition
SICK LEAVE

1. Continuous employment: Each full and complete year of continuous employment is defined for purposes of this entire Article as continuous employment without absence of more than thirty (30) regular working days during the employee's anniversary year, excluding only paid Holidays, paid Sick Leave, paid Vacations, Annual Military Training, authorized Jury Service, paid Bereavement Leave, Temporary Layoff, and Industrial Injury Leaves of one hundred eighty (180) calendar days or less. Continuous employment is computed from an employee's anniversary date of employment which is defined as the date an employee initially commences work, less the periods of adjustment provided in other Sections of this Article VII. A full and complete year of continuous employment begins on the employee's anniversary date as adjusted according to this Article VII and ends at the completion of the shift immediately preceding the next anniversary date

sections.content: Section B. Sick Leave Allowance

1. Employees as of their date of hire and annually thereafter on their benefit date, shall accrue seven (7) days of regular Sick Leave which may be used if the employee or a member of the immediate family (residing within the same household) is physically or mentally incapacitated. Sick Leave benefits are available the first day of the payroll week during which the anniversary date occurs. If the accrual date occurs during a paid or unpaid absence, the seven (7) days of Sick Leave are not granted until the employee returns to work. However, an employee returning from an unpaid leave of absence requiring a benefit date adjustment will not accrue additional days of regular Sick Leave until reaching the payroll week of the adjusted benefit date. Sick Leave cannot be applied retroactively. For employees with positive sick leave balance, annual Sick Leave balances will be paid at the end of each benefit year at fifty percent (50%) of the unused balance. Regular Sick Leave and approved Extended Paid Time Off must be taken prior to taking one (1) or more days of unpaid leave except as provided for personal and occupational illness and injury leaves. Accrued and unused regular Sick Leave is not paid off at the time of termination.

sections.content: 2. Monthly "Normal Retirement Benefits" under the Plan for participants separating from the Service after November 2, 1985 and retiring effective on or after January 1, 1986 will be computed as the greater of:

ARTICLE XVI
BREAVEMENT PAY Section A. Eligibility and Allowance

1. An employee, upon written application, is paid his or her regular pay rate for up to three (3) days (five (5) days when out of state travel is required), when absent from work because of the death of an immediate family member. The days absent from work may be granted in increments of four (4) hours for a half-day's absence (3.3 hours for third shift), or eight (8) hours (6.5 hours for third shift). ARTICLE XXVIII
UNION SECURITY Section A. Union Membership

1. Any employee covered by this Agreement, who, on the effective date of this Agreement, is a member of the Union shall, thereafter, as a condition of employment, maintain membership in the Union for the duration of this Agreement, to the extent of paying the periodic dues uniformly required as a condition of retaining membership in the Union. No employee shall be considered in default of the obligation to pay dues until after the Union has given the employee and the Employer notice in writing and the employee has failed to pay his or her dues within the period of fifteen (15) days following receipt of such written notice. In the event the employee fails to pay his or her dues within the above-mentioned fifteen (15) day period, the Employer shall terminate his or her employment if so requested by the Union in writing.

Dear Mr. Dodd:
This letter will confirm the parties' understanding concerning a drug-free workplace policy.

The Department of Defense has issued emergency regulations mandating a drug-free workplace including the requirement that the Company certify that its operations are drug-free. Accordingly, effective April 1, 1989, a drug-free workplace policy was implemented including testing based on reasonable suspicion applicable to all Company employees. In addition, the Department of Transportation requires employers to conduct drug and alcohol testing on covered employees in accordance with the Department of Transportation regulations. Employees are also subject to testing when recalled to work from layoff provided such employees have been on layoff for a minimum period of twelve (12) months. Further, employees on the recall list, who are offered a non-bargaining unit position, are subject to pre-employment testing. If an employee tests positive either at the time of recall or rehire, he or she will not be eligible for recall for a twelve (12) month period after which time the employee will be recalled and retested when the first available opening occurs. Testing will be conducted in accordance with the elements outlined in Company Practice 3-0-17. Failure on the part of an employee to cooperate in the program can involve discipline up to termination of employment. Failure of the Company to follow the direction of the government (our customer) can result in the loss of contracts, suspension of progress payments and other penalties.

category_summaries.summary: Raytheon Systems Company (the “Employer”) recognizes ELECTRONIC AND SPACE TECHNICIANS, LOCAL 1553 (the “Union”) as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for all production, maintenance, shop clerical employees in factory areas and all employees in the job classifications listed in the Appendices, employed at specified Employer locations (El Segundo, Fullerton, Newport Beach, Torrance, Long Beach, and the Los Angeles Corporate Headquarters), excluding supervisors and all administrative, professional, engineering, office, confidential, plant protection/security, and Finance Department employees. Recognition extends to a successor or assignee of all or a major part of the Employer. The Employer must provide the Union monthly with lists of employees entering/leaving the bargaining unit and a “Bargaining Unit Tab Run,” and must limit placement of stewards to no more than one (1) Department Steward; Union appointment/removal or changes in business unit/department/shift require advance written notification, and stewards are recognized only upon receipt of an official Union Letter of Certification signed by the Recording Secretary addressed to the relevant Labor Relations Representative (alternates upon official Union letter). Steward certification is effective if in place for at least thirty (30) calendar days, and the Employer may decline recognition of Department/shift stewards exceeding an allowance in Section A with registered/certified mail notice to the Union. Employees who are Union members on the agreement’s effective date must maintain membership for the agreement’s duration; agency-fee obligations apply to covered non-members equivalent to current dues for members, with dues/agency-fee deduction and employer termination only after the Union provides written notice and the employee fails to pay within fifteen (15) days, subject to required authorization forms and deduction only where sufficient net earnings remain (including a pickup from next available earnings unless the Union advises not to deduct). Collected dues/fees must be remitted monthly to the Union’s Financial Secretary, payroll deductions may be automatically discontinued upon the required action with notice to the Union, authorizations continue unless revoked, and the Company explains deductions and advises employees they have until day 31 of employment to complete the deduction authorization form. The Union/agency deduction provisions also include the Employer’s agreement to offer E.A.S.T., Local #1553 the opportunity to represent employees if bargaining-unit work is transferred to a San Diego-area facility.

The Agreement’s term runs “from year to year” and is effective upon commencement of the term specified in Section A-1, remaining in full force during any negotiations for amendment or termination. Either party may terminate, amend, or modify by written notice delivered by hand or overnight delivery given at least sixty (60) calendar days prior to the Agreement’s expiration date; such notice triggers termination and the Agreement becomes void twenty (20) calendar days after receipt by either party. The twenty (20) day termination period may be modified by mutual written agreement, in which case the Agreement expires either at the expiration term in Section A.1 or five (5) calendar days after the date of the mutual agreement, whichever applies. Amendments become effective only on the individual dates agreed upon in writing signed by authorized representatives, and the entire Agreement supersedes all prior understandings. Additionally, certain referenced plan provisions are “frozen” for the duration of the contract, with rules addressing the continued accrual (or lack thereof) and treatment of service allowance payments as of March 30, 1968. Certain side terms require mutual written extension of specific deadlines (e.g., January 5, 2002 and January 25, 2002) and will become effective for the subsequent month after receipt by the appropriate labor relations representative. Finally, this Agreement remains in force only if the Company does not outsource computer operations to a company such as CSC.

The agreement vests exclusive Management authority over plant management, Employer business administration, and directing the work force, including maintaining efficiency and discipline (addressing tardiness, absenteeism, and loafing), enforcing plant rules, and assigning personnel to shifts, overtime, and special work requirements (including security clearances), establishing work processes/standards/schedules/methods, and planning, routing, scheduling, and determining plant/unit operation or shutdown. Management may increase/decrease/rotate staffing, hire, promote, demote, discharge or discipline for cause, assign employees with specific skills/training, and define employee qualifications by knowledge/experience, security clearances, certifications, and other critical skills. It may temporarily or indefinitely pay above established maximum rates when operationally required, and may create/revise/delete job classifications and corresponding job descriptions/rates (with prompt notice to the Senior Business Representative and designated organization; if no agreement is reached within five (5) days, the Employer may implement). Staffing levels and mix are always maintained by the Employer within each classification to cover schedules/operations, with assignments based on qualifications and performance at Management’s discretion; written-restriction reviews must occur within a reasonable time, except where restrictions are permanent (and the Employer may review restrictions at any time). The Employer may limit bargaining-unit work to truly necessary work and advise the Union accordingly, reserves existing rights under the Raytheon Severance Pay Plan and Educational Assistance Program (including amendment/modification/termination), may discipline or discharge for a first violation (with no obligation to retain), and limits non-exempt technical support personnel from performing bargaining-unit work. Specific technical provisions also clarify that Electronic Service Technician classifications perform defined maintenance in production/testing/lab/office areas; source surveillance engineers may perform limited inspection; and users may diagnose/isolate and perform certain component/subassembly work, transport devices for personal use. Continuous measurable improvement activities may be performed as part of normal job duties, and bargaining unit personnel assist in these activities under engineers’ direction; Management will issue guidelines and train supervision on the applicable criteria. Where applicable, Management/Employer action is limited by a cap of may not exceed 25% of bargaining unit employees in a department, after requesting volunteers in affected job classifications, while also retaining the right to maintain a sufficient qualified employee complement to run schedules/operations.

The agreement sets hourly pay and wage rules, including application of shift differentials for hours worked; the swing shift differential is 8% of the employee’s hourly pay rate, and shift differentials generally match the employee’s initial work period rate, including that night shift differentials are included in Holiday pay only for employees assigned to night shifts a majority of the workweek. Overtime is governed by Section E, with time-and-one-half for additional hours worked in the same workday and varying premiums for consecutive hours and for Saturday/Sunday (straight time on Saturday/Sunday up to 40 accumulated straight-time hours, then time-and-one-half; Sunday amounts beyond 40 accumulated straight-time hours paid at double time). Employees receive Holiday premium pay only when eligible (including graveyard shift rules—graveyard employees continuing into a Holiday receive premium pay, but those beginning their workday on the night of the Holiday do not), and when holiday hours are not worked due to injury the employee is also paid for assigned hours unable to be worked. Pay also includes wage increases and premiums: base rate general increases of 3% (labor grades 1–24) on specified dates (April 22, 2006 and April 21, 2007), possible individual increases more frequently than every 16 weeks (if merited), a Working Leader premium of 40¢/hour (included in pay for Sick Leave, Holidays, Vacations, Overtime, Shift Differentials, Jury Duty, Annual Military Training, and Bereavement Pay; applicable to temporary Working Leaders assigned for at least one calendar week, and acting as temporary Working Leader up to 3 weeks at a time), and protections against pay reduction due to signing. Deductions for time off/tardiness/other causes are at 1/10th hour’s pay; employees are paid on a biweekly schedule with a 1-week pay-hold practice. Additional compensation provisions include a $3,000 gross lump sum to active employees on the payroll with pro rata payments, and other role/allowance amounts such as $10.00/hour additional pay for eligible employees with annual salary of $50,000+; Flight pay (cumulative per workday, computed in 15-minute units with fractional units credited as full quarter hours and at least 1 hour when earned, based on defined elapsed flight time) and mileage at the applicable IRS rate plus reimbursement rules; sleeper-cab minimum pay (guarantee of at least 8 hours straight time per workday), $36.00/day meals during actual time away from the plant, lodging reimbursement on layover, and per diem decrementing for conference-paid/meals-paid situations. The agreement also addresses overtime hour “apportionment” balancing (no obligation while an apportionment imbalance is 75 hours or more, with an above-75-hour differential payment rule), and overtime crediting/charging rules for absences up to 2 calendar months (charged for overtime they would have been offered) and beyond 2 months (charged based on the average overtime hours charged in the overtime group during the absence period in excess of 2 months).

Scheduling provisions provide that the normal work schedule is five consecutive 8-hour working days, Monday through Friday, with a workday defined as eight consecutive hours (6-1/2 on the graveyard shift), excluding meal periods, and “consecutive hours” treated as uninterrupted work of more than three hours. The Employer generally will not vary an employee’s normal starting time without good and sufficient reason; changes are to be discussed in advance with the Union Department Steward, and shift start times identify the shift worked (including graveyard shift rules). Overtime eligibility requires that all bargaining unit employees in the appropriate classifications have been offered overtime, and overtime is to be apportioned equitably/fairly by job classification among full-time active employees capable of performing the work, with uniform overtime records posted weekly; two overtime/premium rates cannot be paid for the same hours, and time paid but not worked is handled differently for straight-time versus accumulated straight time calculations (with up to 8 accumulated straight-time hours per day for weekly overtime). Weekend premium overtime applies on Saturday (1st day) and Sunday (2nd day), with notice requirements for weekend/weekday/holiday overtime (end of Thursday shift, start of lunch for weekdays, or 72 hours for holidays), and employees excused from overtime under specified circumstances are not disciplined and are credited up to a maximum of 40 hours per employee in a six-month overtime review interval. The Employer may schedule days off and/or shift times other than normal hours for continuous 24-hour/7-day operations, emergencies, or special conditions; for such assignments, the first and second regularly scheduled days off are treated as Saturday and Sunday, employees receive a minimum of 4 hours work/pay as Report Time (subject to exclusions for certain utility/fire/storm/flood or other employer-uncontrollable conditions), and advance notice of shift changes is at least 10 working days when an employee is required to start earlier than normal, scheduling will continue through completion of the normal shift. Rest periods continue as two 10-minute breaks on day and swing shifts, and additional rest periods may be added for legal compliance after discussion with the Union President; swing/graveyard shifts are not to have shifts changed due to jury duty, and for employees assigned to night court the graveyard shift guideline applies regardless of assigned shift. Additional scheduling/pay rules address run assignments (two employees per run, remain with the truck between terminals unless relieved, minimum 8 hours rest per run, and varying schedules for sleeper-cab runs when on the run and when assigned to the Plant), and for run pay calculation purposes only, each 24-hour workday is divided into three 8-hour periods with specified straight/time-and-one-half/no-pay treatment (no pyramiding/duplication of overtime/premium). Payroll week is Saturday through Friday, paid holidays may be rescheduled to match observed holidays at similar establishments, and reduced hours/shift timing may be scheduled at the Employer’s discretion; mandatory weekend overtime is limited such that employees on three consecutive weekends are not required on the fourth, and mandatory overtime is not required on weekends preceding/following a vacation of at least one week.

Leave provisions cover pay treatment for injuries, holidays, vacation, sick leave, jury duty, bereavement, disability leave, and broader leaves of absence. For injury, the employee receives normal pay for hours worked up to the time of injury. Holiday pay is available only to eligible active employees who were on the payroll on the holiday and worked the full scheduled shift immediately before or after (or otherwise qualify, e.g., on paid vacation, authorized death absence, authorized jury/subpoena attendance, paid sick leave, or occupational-injury absence within 120 calendar days after injury); laid off due to RIF before a holiday or retiring on the regular workday before a holiday also preserves holiday pay. Holiday pay is 8 hours at straight time for day/swing shifts and 6.5 hours at straight time for graveyard shifts, and is not paid to employees who are ineligible (e.g., excluded from holiday pay categories). Vacation is granted to active full-time employees (with annual quantities varying by tenure, e.g., 2 weeks/80 hours, 3 weeks/120 hours, up to 5 weeks/200 hours in later years, plus incremental days thereafter), is scheduled by the Employer with seniority preference, may be taken any workweek days if scheduled/approved, and is available beginning the first day of the payroll week in which earned. Vacation accrual depends on continuous employment length (e.g., rates based on months of employment), is limited by a maximum vacation balance (with accrual ceasing once the cap would be exceeded), has no retroactive accrual after reducing below the maximum, and accrual max includes up to 2× the annual allowance. When earned vacation is not taken, eligible employees may receive in-lieu/pro rata payment (day/swing: 1/12 of the vacation allowance; graveyard: 1/12 of applicable graveyard shift hours), computed at the straight time rate, but pro rata/lump arrangements do not apply to employees who quit, are discharged, or are at the maximum vacation balance; additionally, leave in conjunction with vacation follows the vacation period and includes an extra day off with vacation. Sick leave provides 7 days annually (available only upon the accrual/benefit date and cannot be applied retroactively), for physical/mental incapacity of the employee or an immediate family member in the same household; if accrual occurs during an absence, days are granted upon return, and sick leave is not paid during a leave used to collect holiday pay. Sick leave pay is straight time and applies in a minimum 2-hour increment with further increments of 0.1 hour, with advance approval required for sick leave under 4 hours, and working leader premiums are included; accrued unused regular sick leave is paid out at 50% at end of each benefit year, but unused regular sick leave is not paid off at termination. Extended Paid Time Off/extended paid disability requires medical certification and approval, provides extended disability coverage (with the note that extended sick leave may be used without first using regular sick leave if authorized), and payments are reduced/integrated by State disability benefits or other Company disability insurance. Jury duty provisions include pay at the employee’s pay rate (including shift premium if applicable) for up to 3 days, with conditions on frequency and exclusions (e.g., jury service while on leave/sick/vacation; not obligated beyond Company terms), notice requirements (summons notice at least 10 working days prior; failure disqualifies benefits), and obligations regarding returning to work when service is shorter than 4 hours. Bereavement is paid (including 8 hours’ holiday-style pay in the relevant portion of the agreement) for death of an immediate family member, subject to supervision approval and authorization for use. The agreement also provides for unpaid personal leaves for acceptable reasons, pregnancy-related disability leave applications subject to law, medical leave of absence upon disability approval with potential medical layoff and COBRA eligibility if unable to return after 24 months, and other leaves of absence that follow specified scheduling rules (e.g., leave follows vacation; adjusted anniversary dates for absences beyond 30 regular working days, with limitations on credited periods). The provisions include rules about termination/benefit computation using the last day actually worked, extended leave following sick leave in certain scenarios, restrictions on taking sick leave for regularly scheduled days off (6th/7th day), leave-administration documentation, and an additional paid time off (PTO) framework for employees subject to the referenced PTO terms (including advance of PTO days each January 1, carryover limits up to 5 days and use-by dates, and that bereavement/jury/military reserve duty are not charged to PTO).

Healthcare provisions provide that time on Extended Sick Leave (including regular Sick Leave) counts as waiting time under disability plans, and job-incurred illnesses or injuries are covered by disability benefits in accordance with applicable Workers’ Compensation laws. During the contract term, eligible employees (and eligible dependents) are offered Medical Plan coverage, including either a Medical Plan or an HMO, with each employee permitted to elect only one plan; plan designs for POS/HMO/PPO are the same as the salaried population’s 2005 designs and remain “frozen” for the contract. Employee medical premium contributions are the lesser of negotiated maximums or the salaried employee contribution rate; enrolled employees contribute on a pre-tax basis. A Vision Care Plan is also continued for active employees at no additional premium, with exams every 12 months and lenses/frames every 24 months, and specified copayments (e.g., $10 for an exam; up to $20 maximum per person for lenses/frames). Two STD plans and two LTD plans are offered using the same plan design and contribution level as salaried employees, and retiree medical coverage is continued for retirees until age 65 (with continued coverage for eligible spouses until age 65, dependent children through age 19 or 25 if full-time students, and no age limit for totally disabled dependent children meeting tax dependent requirements). Medical deductibles for retirees match active employees, retiree medical is administered by the Employer, and HMO continuity at retirement is permitted. Additional Medicare Supplemental coverage is available to eligible retirees over age 65 who retire on/after January 1, 1999, with employer administration and retirees paying the selected monthly premium. Healthcare cost-sharing during approved medical leave is set for the first 12 months (company pays medical/vision and dental insurance) and the second 12 months (employee pays at the employee contribution rate). Flexible Spending Accounts (health care and dependent care) are offered, allowing annual deferrals up to $5,000 of base pay, with the Company bearing administrative expenses, and the plans may be amended or terminated to maintain legal compliance.

Under the Ancillary benefits, the Employer will make available (on the same basis as for salaried employees) an Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance Plan for the contract duration, with a Basic Plan benefit of 50% of weekly base pay to age 65 and a Plus Plan benefit of 60% of weekly base pay to age 65. During annual enrollment, employees may increase coverage by up to one (1) times their Annual Base salary without proof of insurability. The Employer will also provide two Flexible Spending Accounts (health care reimbursement and a dependent care reimbursement account on the same basis as salaried employees) each year for the contract term, including an option to defer up to $5,000 of base pay for allowable dependent care expenses, payable through equal payroll deductions, and FSA debit cards for health care reimbursement account use in lieu of reimbursement. Retirement-related ancillary provisions include making qualified retirement, savings and investment, and stock ownership plans available to eligible covered employees during the agreement term; requiring participant contributions of 3% of compensation for the Retirement Plan; and providing a Summary Plan Description to employees. The retirement benefits include a special layoff provision for employees age 50+ within five years of the “Rule of 75,” providing a benefit equal to accrued benefits reduced by 1.5% per month retirement occurs prior to the “Rule of 75” date, and retiree life insurance coverage. A non-contributory benefit applies to employees hired/rehired after November 2, 1991 (superseding the contributory benefit), and earlier laid-off employees recalled within five years of layoff had 30 days to choose between contributory and non-contributory benefits. For those employed by Raytheon on/after May 23, 2005, pensions use the Guaranteed Pension Formula, and pensions may be adjusted when starting under different payment forms or before the social security retirement date. The Raytheon Savings and Investment Plan will be made available to eligible employees, allowing participation upon hire; employee contributions between 1% and 50% in 1% increments of qualifying compensation (base weekly wages, supplemental wage payments, and overtime); with company matching invested alongside employee contributions. Company matching based on the first 4% made before 07/01/05 must remain in Raytheon Common Stock for five full plan years after the contribution plan year, after which participants may transfer the common stock value to other options; and participants may take lump-sum distributions of their account(s). The Employer will extend the Stock Ownership Plan to all eligible employees, with a company contribution equal to 1/2% of eligible earnings allocated in the following year, with the contribution terminating for the pay period that includes July 1, 2005. For employees represented by E.A.S.T., Local 1553, severance pay and participation in the Educational Assistance Program continue on the same basis and under the same terms and conditions as those programs.

The contract contains protections against improper use of non-bargaining work and staffing: salaried/non-bargaining employees must not regularly perform bargaining-unit work, and the Company agrees not to use contract or other arrangements to circumvent bargaining-unit classifications or reduce the bargaining unit size. During layoffs, bargaining-unit employees are protected by limits on contract staffing—no contract employee may perform bargaining-unit work in a affected classification longer than 90 calendar days, contract employees in affected areas must be removed before bargaining-unit layoff notices, and the Company will not use contract labor to replace laid-off unit employees without offering recall first. Recall must follow seniority order, with the “date of recall” being the date the recalled employee actually starts work, and eligible laid-off employees must be offered recall in order of seniority. Laid-off employees may decline short temporary recall assignments of 90 calendar days or less without losing recall rights; if a junior accepts and the assignment exceeds 90 days, the employee may be retained without re-offering to more senior employees who previously declined. Layoff/displacement rules provide for bumping/displacement within the bargaining unit and across directly related, lower-paid classifications (subject to conditions), and specify retention tie-breakers when seniority dates, company service dates, and hire dates are identical. Temporary layoffs not exceeding 12 weeks in any 12-month period may be conducted with the least bargaining-unit seniority in the directly affected section, while temporary-layoff employees generally continue to accumulate seniority (except probationary employees). Additional seniority administration provisions address continuous employment definitions, probation periods (including a 90-day probation for certain new/rehired employees), recall/probationary rules when employees accept jobs outside their recall classification, consequences for failing to timely return to work (removal from recall lists and loss of seniority/recall rights), and preferential seniority provisions for designated stewards/union officers to avoid unnecessary steward dislocation. Separate rules also govern job-classification conversions, seniority pools, and preferential reemployment for specified successor classifications, including conditions tied to passing required exams and the effect of refusing preferential reemployment on future recall eligibility.

Training and progression occur in eight (8)-week intervals, with Trainees reclassified when their base rate equals the minimum of the Job Classification for which they are being trained. The attached job descriptions govern the specific skills required for each new (successor) job classification, and incumbent employees are credited with core/non-core skills depending on their MS level: MS “A” (1 core and 2 non-core), MS “B” (2 non-core), and MS “C” (1 non-core). For Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Mechanic L/G 23 incumbents, there is a $500 award for each core skill obtained, capped at 2 core skills. OJT assignments may be made by management during the employee’s tenure, and employees may be assigned to work within the full scope of their job classification if provided appropriate orientation/training; however, training/OJT is not the sole basis for upgrading to a higher classification. Finally, individual employee rates require approval by the Joint Apprenticeship Committee.

The Disputes/Grievance provisions provide for a structured role of Department and Senior Stewards (including limits on Department Stewards at no more than 1 per 80 bargaining unit employees by shift within each Division, and up to 12 Senior Stewards—no more than 5 appointed by the Union—restricted to the Raytheon El Segundo North and South facilities), with Union Officers barred from serving as Stewards or participating in the grievance process. Stewards (including alternates and temporary coverage for absentee certified Stewards) may investigate grievances with unannounced access to restricted areas, subject to certifications, shift/area limitations, supervisory permission to leave work (not unreasonably withheld), and a cap of no more than 2 hours per month per appointed Steward for such grievance-handling activity. Grievance processing follows time-bound steps: a First Step meeting is requested within 5 working days after the event(s), scheduled within an additional 5 working days, and involves the employee and Department/Senior Steward; Step Two requires filing/placement into Step Two and a Step Two meeting within 5 working days after the Company receives the written grievance, with the Company providing a written answer within 5 working days and failure to answer timely allowing the Union to proceed. General grievances, layoff/discharge grievances (filed within 10 working days), and certain disputes are directed to specified processing or direct arbitration; grievances settled at Step One are not precedent setting and are “without prejudice.” If not resolved, the Union may appeal by mutual agreement to a Designated Organization Grievance Resolution Committee (meeting within 30 working days, written answer within 5 working days), and then may submit to informal arbitration by providing notices within specified windows (e.g., within 10 working days after receipt of the Step Two answer; and generally within 15 or 20 working days depending on the triggering document). Arbitration selection procedures include alternate-strike/coin-toss from a blind random panel (including an expedited process for discharge and layoffs with a 90-day hearing-date target), binding decisions based only on the Agreement’s existing provisions, and fee allocation where the parties contribute equally unless postponement results in assessed fees/expenses to the requesting party. Additional limits include: certain matters are excluded from the grievance procedure (e.g., apprenticeship standards and specified classification-range issues), probationary employee terminations are generally not subject to the grievance procedure (with supervisory notice requirements, including prompt notice for immediate terminations), and no retroactive effect is permitted beyond 11 working days prior to the verbal complaint.

The parties commit to maintaining high safety and workmanship standards, including systematic and regular safety inspections, housekeeping/cleaning as necessary for safety and cleanliness, and the provision of modern safety devices and protective equipment (use is mandatory when furnished). Smoking privileges are to be governed by clearly communicated plant regulations. The Employer will address on-the-job hazards arising from emergency response operations and ensure compliance with state and federal workers’ compensation laws. Unsafe job assignments must be reported to the immediate supervisor, who must investigate immediately; a Safety Engineer will determine the outcome and the Employer may suspend unsafe work operations. Physical examinations and employer-imposed medical restrictions (with review dates tied to severity) may be required, and continued work permission is at the Employer doctor’s discretion. A Safety Steward is to be appointed to the relevant committee through recommendations by the Senior Business Representative. The agreement also provides for drug-free workplace and substance-abuse measures, including pre-employment/testing on recall/rehire, testing based on reasonable suspicion, and consequences: an employee who tests positive at recall or rehire is ineligible for recall for twelve (12) months, and failure to cooperate with the program may result in discipline up to termination; the approach emphasizes rehabilitation over punishment. Smoking, testing, and employment decisions are also subject to non-discrimination obligations by both parties.

Miscellany provisions include: (1) labor peace—no strikes, lockouts, sympathy strikes, slow-downs, sit-downs, work stoppages, or other job actions by either the Union or its members, and no comparable individual or general suspension/stoppage of work by either party; (2) grievance/discipline limitations—no time during working hours for soliciting grievances, and no strike/job action while disputes/grievances are being processed under the Grievance Procedure or Arbitration; (3) Union access/activities—no soliciting of Union members, dues, or other Union activities on Company property during working hours; Union notices must be signed by an authorized Union officer and posted by the Senior Steward, with the Union providing the Company quarterly (in writing) the currently certified stewards and the Company posting them on Union bulletin boards; (4) reporting and caps on contract employees—the Company provides by the 15th of each month a report listing departments, occupations, and the names of contract employees performing bargaining-unit work, with the total number of contract employees capped at 30, and the cap not applying to contract employees performing custodian or relocation work; after a 2-month implementation grace period, the Company forfeits the right to add any additional contract employees for the next 12-month period; (5) administrative housekeeping—employees on leave of absence must keep their Business Unit Human Resources Department informed of address/telephone; lodging expenses (where applicable) require receipts; (6) grievance/Union-related cooperation and accountability—both parties cooperate on required submissions, each party pays its own obligations under the section, and the Union indemnifies/holds the Employer harmless for liabilities or expenses incurred by the Employer from these Union-related activities; and (7) miscellaneous supplemental/collateral terms—supplemental agreements are incorporated by reference (including temporary assignments and business leave terms), specific procedures for stewards leaving the job and using voicemail/written notice if the supervisor is unavailable, and provisions governing a source-inspection/prototype function (including limits where employees refuse assistance), plus rules for interviewing on Company time requiring prior permission and status information post-interview.
